prp.objective: Create test/settingsLoader.test.ts — the vitest regression guard for src/settingsLoader.ts's merge + trust-gate + never-throw contract (dependency P1.M1.T1.S1, status Complete). The test imports loadMulliganSettings from ../src/settingsLoader.js, drives every branch with tmp-dir fixtures (mirroring test/log.test.ts), and asserts: (a) global-only mulligan returned; (b) local-only mulligan returned when isTrusted:true; (c) BOTH present + isTrusted:true → LOCAL mulligan WINS (top-level REPLACE, NOT deep-merge — the precedence regression guard); (d) isTrusted:false/undefined → local file NEVER read (global returned even when a local file exists); (e) neither file present → undefined; (f) malformed JSON → exactly one console.warn per malformed file with the '[mulligan] settings: <path> unreadable:' prefix, then falls through; (g) file present but no 'mulligan' key (incl. non-object top-level) → undefined; (h) never throws on any adversarial input. PLUS the pinned non-object .mulligan behavior (S1 returns 42 / 'off' / null AS-IS, not validated) and the consumer contract (loadMulliganSettings()===undefined → validateConfig(undefined) deepEquals DEFAULT_CONFIG). settingsLoader is STATELESS (no module cache) so vi.resetModules() is NOT required; redirect the global path via vi.mock('node:os') (SPIKED working). This is a pure test-only task: it touches ONLY test/settingsLoader.test.ts and must NOT modify src/settingsLoader.ts, src/config.ts, or src/index.ts.
implementationSteps: CREATE test/settingsLoader.test.ts. Imports (mirror test/log.test.ts + test/config.test.ts): `import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from "vitest";` `import { mkdtempSync, rmSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";` `import { tmpdir, homedir } from "node:os";` `import { join } from "node:path";` `import { loadMulliganSettings } from "../src/settingsLoader.js";` `import { DEFAULT_CONFIG, validateConfig } from "../src/config.js";`. Note the .js specifiers (repo ESM/Bundler convention) and that src/config.js is imported for the consumer-contract assertions only.

Redirect the global path via vi.mock("node:os"): declare `let mockHome: string = "/nonexistent-initial";` then `vi.mock("node:os", async (importOriginal) => { const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import("node:os")>(); return { ...actual, homedir: () => mockHome }; });` and a `function setHome(dir: string): void { mockHome = dir; }`. vi.mock is hoisted by vitest so the module-under-test picks up the redirected homedir (SPIKED working in vitest 1.6.1). Keep tmpdir and other node:os exports intact via importOriginal. Capture `const originalHomedir = homedir;` for type reference only.

Add two tmp dirs per test in beforeEach/afterEach (mirror test/log.test.ts): `let home: string; let cwd: string;` `beforeEach(() => { home = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mulligan-sl-home-")); cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mulligan-sl-cwd-")); setHome(home); });` `afterEach(() => { rmSync(home, { recursive: true, force: true }); rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true }); });`. DO NOT add vi.resetModules() — settingsLoader is stateless (research note §3 + external_deps §9).

Add a writeSettings(dir, relPath, data) helper: compute `const filePath = join(dir, relPath);` mkdirSync the parent with {recursive:true} (slice on last "/"), then `writeFileSync(filePath, typeof data === "string" ? data : JSON.stringify(data), "utf8")`. relPath values: ".pi/agent/settings.json" for the global file (under home) and ".pi/settings.json" for the local file (under cwd).
Write case (b) local-only trusted: home empty; writeSettings(cwd,".pi/settings.json",{mulligan:{maxDepth:9}}); expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:true})).toEqual({maxDepth:9}).

Write case (c) BOTH → LOCAL WINS (the precedence regression guard): writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",{mulligan:{a:1}}); writeSettings(cwd,".pi/settings.json",{mulligan:{b:2}}); expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:true})).toEqual({b:2}) — assert it is NOT {a:1,b:2} (no deep-merge). Add a sub-case: local mulligan:null wins over global → writeSettings(home,...,{mulligan:{x:1}}); writeSettings(cwd,...,{mulligan:null}); expect(...).toBeNull() (hasOwnProperty → null is a present key).

Write case (d) isTrusted false AND undefined: both files have mulligan; expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:false})).toEqual(GLOBAL) AND expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd})).toEqual(GLOBAL) — the local file is NEVER read when isTrusted !== true (two sub-asserts or two cases).
Write case (e) neither file present: fresh tmp dirs; expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:true})).toBeUndefined().

Write case (f) malformed JSON: (f1) global malformed — writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json","{ not json"); writeSettings(cwd,".pi/settings.json",{mulligan:{local:true}}); `const warn = vi.spyOn(console,"warn").mockImplementation(()=>{});` try { expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:true})).toEqual({local:true}); expect(warn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); const globalPath = join(home,".pi","agent","settings.json"); expect(warn.mock.calls[0][0]).toContain("[mulligan] settings:"); expect(warn.mock.calls[0][0]).toContain(globalPath); expect(warn.mock.calls[0][0]).toContain("unreadable:"); } finally { warn.mockRestore(); }. (f2) local malformed (trusted, global valid) → returns global; warn fires once containing the LOCAL path. ALSO a missing-file case: spy console.warn; expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:true})).toBeUndefined(); expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled() (ENOENT is silent).

Write case (g) no mulligan key / non-object top-level: writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",[1,2,3]); writeSettings(cwd,".pi/settings.json","42"); expect(loadMulliganSettings({cwd,isTrusted:true})).toBeUndefined(). ALSO unrelated-keys-not-leaked: writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",{packages:[{name:"mulligan"}],defaultModel:"gpt-4",mulligan:{enabled:true}}); expect(loadMulliganSettings()).toEqual({enabled:true}) — packages/defaultModel NOT returned.

Write the PINNED non-object .mulligan case (S1 returns it AS-IS): writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",{mulligan:42}); expect(loadMulliganSettings()).toBe(42); then rmSync the file and writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",{mulligan:"off"}); expect(loadMulliganSettings()).toBe("off"). (config.ts:validateConfig coerces non-record raw later; the loader does NOT validate.)

Write the CONSUMER CONTRACT cases: (1) no files → const result = loadMulliganSettings(); expect(result).toBeUndefined(); expect(validateConfig(result)).toEqual(DEFAULT_CONFIG). (2) {mulligan:null} → writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",{mulligan:null}); const result = loadMulliganSettings(); expect(result).toBeNull(); expect(validateConfig(result)).toEqual(DEFAULT_CONFIG). Import DEFAULT_CONFIG + validateConfig from ../src/config.js. Do NOT call setConfig (it would mutate cachedConfig and force vi.resetModules).

Write the opts-omitted case: writeSettings(home,".pi/agent/settings.json",{mulligan:{rewind:{maxDepth:3}}}); expect(loadMulliganSettings()).toEqual({rewind:{maxDepth:3}}) (isTrusted undefined → no local read, global-only). Assert it does not throw.
Run Level 1 gate: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (the repo's only type/style tool — no eslint/ruff configured; baseline verified exit 0).
Run Level 2 gate: `npx vitest run test/settingsLoader.test.ts` — all cases green. Run Level 3 gate: `npm test` — full suite GREEN, 0 regressions.

HONOR scope boundaries (manual, not shell gates per G1.2): do NOT modify src/settingsLoader.ts (S1, Complete), src/config.ts, or src/index.ts (P1.M1.T2.S1); the test must NOT import @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; do NOT add vi.resetModules(); do NOT delete the test file or any spike after verifying (G1.4 — throwaway artifacts survive the coder's turn; cleanup is manual/post-validation). successCriteria.description: test/settingsLoader.test.ts exists and imports loadMulliganSettings from ../src/settingsLoader.js (plus DEFAULT_CONFIG + validateConfig from ../src/config.js for the consumer-contract assertions).
Case (a) global-only: a global file with a mulligan block is returned verbatim.
Case (b) local-only trusted: a local-only file with isTrusted:true is returned verbatim.

Case (c) BOTH present + isTrusted:true → LOCAL mulligan WINS via top-level REPLACE (assert the local object, e.g. {b:2}, NOT a deep-merge {a:1,b:2}); also local mulligan:null wins over global (hasOwnProperty → null is present).
Case (d) isTrusted:false AND isTrusted:undefined → local file is NEVER read; global value is returned even when a local file exists.
Case (e) neither file present → returns undefined.

Case (f) malformed JSON → exactly one console.warn per malformed file with the '[mulligan] settings: <path> unreadable:' prefix (asserted via vi.spyOn + warn.mock.calls), then falls through to the other file or undefined; a MISSING file emits NO warn (ENOENT is silent).

Case (g) file present but no mulligan key (incl. non-object top-level like [1,2,3] or 42) → undefined; unrelated top-level keys (packages, defaultModel) are NOT leaked — only the mulligan value is returned.
Case (h) never throws on any malformed/adversarial input — each adversarial call wrapped in expect(()=>...).not.toThrow().
Pinned non-object .mulligan behavior: {mulligan:42}→42 and {mulligan:"off"}→"off" returned AS-IS (S1 does not validate/coerce).
Consumer contract: loadMulliganSettings()===undefined → validateConfig(undefined) deepEquals DEFAULT_CONFIG; AND {mulligan:null} → returns null → validateConfig(null) deepEquals DEFAULT_CONFIG.
vi.mock("node:os") redirects homedir() at a fresh tmp dir per test so the global path is hermetic (the real ~/.pi/agent/settings.json is never read).
vi.resetModules() is NOT used (settingsLoader is stateless); console.warn spies are restored in a finally/afterEach so they don't leak.
Scope honored: src/settingsLoader.ts, src/config.ts, and src/index.ts are NOT modified by this test-only task (S1 / P1.M1.T2.S1 own them); the test does not import @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
All three validation gates pass: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json (exit 0); npx vitest run test/settingsLoader.test.ts (all cases green); npm test (full suite green, zero regressions).
